newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK consortium in HK$40 bln skyscraper project.
newsitem.headline: HK consortium in HK$40 bln skyscraper project.

text.p: A Hong Kong consortium said on Wednesday it will develop a waterfront office and retail project which will give Hong Kong a world class landmark and put it on par with cities like Paris and New York.
The HK$40 billion Hong Kong Station development, featuring an 88-storey office building with an observatory, is being undertaken by Central Waterfront Property Development Ltd.
The consortium groups Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd with 47.5 percent, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd with 32.5 percent, and Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd with 15 percent.
Sun Chung Estate Co Ltd, a member of the Bank of China group, holds the remaining five percent.
Officials at a news conference said the project will put Hong Kong in the same league as cities like Paris and New York.

"A plan for an observation tower on top of the tallest of the towers (88 storeys) has been proposed, which could provide Hong Kong with its own unique identifying landmark on a par with the Empire State Building in New York or the Eiffel Tower in Paris," said Eric Tung, a director of Central Waterfront.
The project also has a 38-storey office building, an 800,000 square foot shopping mall, hotels, luxury service apartments, and leisure facilities covering 140,000 square feet.
The two office towers will provide a total 2.73 million square feet of office space.

Half of the total investment goes to the land, a prestigious harbour-front plot in Central district which lies on top of the terminus of the airport railway which will link Hong Kong island to the new Chek Lap Kok airport, due to open in 1998.

Consortium officials dismissed long-standing protests from grassroot groups which have criticised the 88-storey building as further congesting the harbour front and an eyesore which will obstruct the view of the famous Peak on Hong Kong island.

"As far as we know, there are no objections to the height of our building," said Tung. "We've got a very famous architect to design the building and it will add to the beautiful skyline of Hong Kong," he said.
The development will be built in four phases. The 38-storied block, part of phase one, will be completed by end 1998. The whole project is slated for completion in 2004.
